chunks: From him, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabii, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you think about exchanging red dates and fresh dates, one for one? He said: 'There is no objection.' I said: And what about buckthorn and grapes, one for one? He said: 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.التَّمْر: Dates (dried fruit of the date palm)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to trade different types of fruits like dates and grapes in equal measure according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of *mithlan bi-mithl* (equal measure) exchange for diverse fruit varieties, distinguishing them from the stricter rules of *riba al-fadl* applicable to staple commodities. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that the prohibition of excess in barter does not extend to all perishable goods, provided the exchange is immediate and equal in weight or measure, thereby facilitating daily trade while avoiding usury.
